chunks: Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a woman who menstruates once every three years: how should she observe her waiting period?

He عليه السلام said: “She should consider the menstrual cycles she used to have when her menstruation was regular, and let her observe a waiting period of three menstrual cycles. Then let her marry, if she wishes.”

key_terms.الِاسْتِقَامَةِ: the time of regularity and normal menstrual pattern
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ: three menstrual cycles constituting the waiting period here
key_terms.قُرُوئِهَا: her menstrual cycles used as the basis for calculating 'iddah
key_terms.لْتَتَزَوَّجْ: let her marry after completing the prescribed waiting period

ai.seo_question: How does a woman with extremely irregular menstruation observe her waiting period in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the waiting period of a divorced woman whose menstruation has become extremely infrequent. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that her 'iddah be calculated according to the pattern of her normal past cycles during the time of regularity, counting three menstrual cycles before remarriage.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4803 - Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a woman who menstruates once every three years-how should she observe her waiting period?

Imam (as) said: "She should consider the usual menstruation cycles she used to have when her menstruation was regular and observe a waiting period of three menstrual cycles. Then, if she wishes, she may marry."
